blocks.x: Winnipeg building owners can't always count on rent growth alone to protect income. The other lever is cost. If you want to reduce operating costs in a commercial building, the right commercial property renovation can lower energy, maintenance and turnover costs year after year.
Here are 12 upgrades that can pay back, grouped by where the savings come from.
Energy: Winnipeg winters make this a big lever

**1. Windows and doors.** Failed seals, single-pane glass and drafty doors can drive heating bills up through a Manitoba winter and cause [condensation problems](/blog/window-condensation-winnipeg-winter).

**2. Air sealing and insulation.** Attics, rim joists, roof assemblies and wall penetrations are common leak points in older buildings. Before you start, review how the work can affect indoor air quality, as [Efficiency Manitoba advises](https://efficiencymb.ca/business/building-envelope/), and [test suspect old insulation for asbestos](/blog/asbestos-testing-before-renovating-manitoba).
**3. LED lighting with controls.** Corridors, stairwells, parkades and exterior lights run long hours. LEDs with occupancy sensors can cut energy and maintenance.
**4. Heating system tune-ups and controls.** Have your heating contractor service boilers and furnaces, and add smarter controls to avoid heating empty or unoccupied space.
**5. Water-saving fixtures.** Low-flow toilets, showerheads and aerators can reduce water and sewer costs in multi-unit buildings.
Maintenance: spend once, not every year
**6. Durable flooring.** [Commercial-grade vinyl plank or tile](/services/flooring) in high-traffic areas can outlast carpet.
**7. Masonry repairs.** [Repointing and repairing brick](/services/masonry-stucco) before freeze-thaw damage spreads can prevent much larger repairs later.
**8. Standardized finishes.** One paint colour, one flooring, one fixture package across units can make repairs faster and simpler.
**9. Leak detection.** Sensors and shutoff valves under sinks and water heaters can stop small leaks from becoming major damage claims.
Leasing and retention: reduce vacancy

**10. Common-area refresh.** Lobbies, corridors and entrances shape how tenants feel about a building every day. See these [lobby renovation ideas borrowed from hotels](/blog/apartment-lobby-renovation-ideas).
**11. Unit or suite updates at turnover.** [Kitchens](/services/kitchen-renovations), [bathrooms](/services/bathroom-renovations) and flooring done during a vacancy can reduce future vacant days.
**12. Accessibility improvements.** Power door operators, ramps and accessible washrooms can widen your pool of tenants and customers.
Use Efficiency Manitoba incentives

[Efficiency Manitoba](https://efficiencymb.ca/business/) offers programs for commercial and multi-unit buildings. Its [Commercial Deep Energy Retrofit Program](https://efficiencymb.ca/business/deep-energy-retrofit/), for example, supports projects that cut a building's energy use by at least 20%, with up to $12,000 toward energy modelling and a performance incentive of $2.25 to $6.00 per square foot depending on savings.

Applications must be approved **before** work starts. Separate programs such as the [Building Envelope Program](https://efficiencymb.ca/business/building-envelope/), Business Lighting Program and HVAC & Controls are also available, each with its own rules. The Building Envelope Program, for one, requires a contractor registered with Efficiency Manitoba. Check [efficiencymb.ca](https://efficiencymb.ca/business/) for current details, or see our [commercial rebates guide](/blog/efficiency-manitoba-commercial-rebates).
How to prioritize upgrades that reduce operating costs
Get an energy assessment or review your utility bills to find the biggest losses.

Fix the envelope (windows, doors, air sealing) before upsizing mechanical equipment. [Significant envelope alterations](https://legacy.winnipeg.ca/ppd/Documents/Permits/CommercialAlterationDesignSummary/Guide-Commercial-Alteration-Design-Summary.pdf) in a larger building (Part 3 of the building code) can need an architect or engineer.

Plan early. A [project enrolled in the Commercial Deep Energy Retrofit Program](https://efficiencymb.ca/wp-content/uploads/EM_Commercial-Deep-Energy-Retrofit-Program-Guide.pdf) generally gives up prescriptive incentives from other Efficiency Manitoba programs for the same planned upgrades, so compare the two routes before you apply.
Schedule exterior work for the warmer months, interior work year-round.
The bottom line
A well-planned commercial property renovation can help protect income when rent growth is limited: lower bills, fewer emergency repairs and fewer vacancies.
